cases.question: How do I enter players on my roster?
cases.answer:
To enter players on your roster:

1. From your Captain Dashboard, go to Captain Tools.
2. Click Manage Roster.
3. Click Add Player.
4. In the pop-up, your home community is preselected; use the drop-down to view available players, their eligibility status, and DUPR ratings.
5. Select the player and click Add Player to Team.

If a player is missing a DUPR ID or Season Rating, you can still select the player and click Add Player to Team; League Management will be automatically notified to review the issue and update you on the player’s status.

If a player is marked “Not Eligible,” attempting to add them will show an on-screen message explaining the specific reason why.

cases.question: How can I update my roster?
cases.answer:
To update your roster, go to your Captain Dashboard, open Captain Tools, and click Manage Roster. From there you can add, change, or remove players.

cases.question: How do I enter match scores?

evidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide

cases.answer:
To enter match scores:

1. Open the match and click the red “Enter Match Scores” button. It is available only on or after the scheduled match date.
2. Use the dropdowns to select the players for each game, normally using “Use this saved team” / the Match Setup players. If there were lineup changes, select the correct player from the individual player dropdown.
3. Enter the scores in each game block.
4. Click Submit. The system will check for errors before saving.
5. The opposing captain then receives a verification request and must open the match to verify the scores or dispute them. The visiting team captain must verify promptly so results can be reviewed and entered into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

Important exceptions: for individual game forfeits or retirements, refer to the official League Rules when entering those results. If the entire match date is forfeited, canceled, or cannot be played due to weather or scheduling conflicts, do not enter it in the system; notify League Management at info@lwrpickleballclub.com. If a line has an eligibility issue, an ineligible player cannot be selected and score fields are blocked.

sources.citation: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS — Page 13
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide — ENTER/VERIFY SCORES — Page 9

cases.question: How does Rally Scoring work?

evidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

cases.answer:
Rally Scoring in the LWR DUPR League works this way:

- A team can win a point whether it is serving or receiving, except for the game-winning point.
- If the serving team loses a rally, it is a side out: the opposing team gets a point and takes over the serve.
- After a side out, the server is based on that team’s score: right-side player serves on an even score; left-side player serves on an odd score.
- Players switch sides only after winning a point on their own serve, and the same player continues serving from the new side.
- When a team reaches one point below the game-winning score, its score freezes. That team may score the game-winning point only while serving. Example: in a game to 25, the freeze begins at 24.
- The freeze applies only to the team that reached the freeze point; the other team continues normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches its freeze point.
- In win-by-two games, if the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, both teams become unfrozen and normal Rally Scoring resumes. Scores freeze again whenever a team reaches a score where its next point would win by two. This continues until one team wins by two, and the game-winning point must always be scored while serving.

cases.question: How does Rally Scoring work in a Picklebreaker?

evidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

cases.answer:
In a Picklebreaker using Rally Scoring:

- A team can win a point whether it is serving or receiving, except for the game-winning point.
- If the serving team loses a rally, it is a side out: the opposing team gets a point and takes over the serve.
- After a side out, the first server is based on that team’s score: right-side player serves if the score is even; left-side player serves if the score is odd.
- Players switch sides only after winning a point on their own serve, and the same player keeps serving from the new side.
- When a team reaches one point below the game-winning score, its score freezes. From that point, that team can score the game-winning point only while serving.
- In a win-by-two game, if the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, both teams unfreeze and normal Rally Scoring resumes. This freeze/unfreeze process continues as needed until one team wins by two points. The game-winning point must always be scored while serving.

cases.question: How is my Season DUPR calculated?

evidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

cases.answer:
Your Season DUPR Rating is established on the date communicated to all captains before the first scheduled league match, and it stays in effect for the entire season.

How it is calculated/applied:
- DUPR ratings are truncated to the nearest tenth to establish the Season DUPR Rating. Example provided: 3.496 becomes 3.4.
- If your DUPR Reliability Factor is below 29, you are classified as “Not Rated” for league purposes.
- For team aggregate rating calculations, an NR player is initially assigned the division’s maximum individual DUPR rating minus 0.5.
- If you are rostered in multiple divisions, the highest adjusted Season DUPR Rating assigned to you is used across all divisions where you appear.
- Some leagues use the Age-based DUPR sub-rating; if a player has not established a 65+ Age-based rating by the start of the season, their 50+ Age-based rating is used.
